title: Internal Audit Manager
description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world's biggest financial problems. We're looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Internal Audit team helps Robinhood meet a complex set of global regulations for crypto-assets and payment services. Our mission is to give the Board of Directors, its Committees and company leadership independent, objective and timely assurance that our governance, risk management and internal controls work as intended, so we can spot new risks early and keep strengthening our control environment! As Internal Audit Manager , you will lead and carry out audits of Operations, Compliance and Technology across our crypto business, in line with the Internal Audit plan. You will work with Internal Audit leadership to identify risks, document and test controls, and recommend improvements, and you will help share risk information between the regulated entities, Robinhood Markets (RHM) leadership and the Board. This role is based in our Luxembourg office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Plan and run audits of Operations, Compliance and Technology processes in our crypto business, from scoping through final reporting, in line with the Internal Audit plan. Perform walkthroughs, control testing and substantive testing, and prepare work papers, flowcharts, narratives and risk and control matrices (RCMs) that document your procedures, findings and conclusions. Write clear audit findings that state the issue, its root cause and its business impact, and agree on recommendations with the teams you audit and with leadership. Build RCMs for new audit areas, focusing on the controls that best reduce the highest risks, and assess whether policies, procedures and systems are adequate and efficient. Work with Business, Risk, Compliance, Legal and Technology partners to understand their processes, solve problems and recommend process improvements, while managing several audits and ad hoc requests at once. What you bring 7+ years of external or internal audit experience at a company that provides financial products or services, including evaluating internal controls or compliance programs. Experience assessing the design and effectiveness of controls at a crypto exchange, market maker, custody provider, broker-dealer or similar financial institution, and working knowledge of crypto-asset regulations. Broker-dealer regulation knowledge is a plus. Experience supporting regulatory examinations, including preparing for them and responding to regulator questions and findings. A bachelor's degree in Audit, Finance, Operations or Technology, or equivalent practical experience. Certifications such as Certified Internal Auditor (CIA) or Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA), or crypto and brokerage certifications, are a plus. Proficiency in written and spoken English, strong analytical and problem-solving skills, and the ability to manage multiple projects on time in a fast-changing, regulated, international setting. Occasional travel is required. What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, and bonus programs Top tier benefits to fuel your work, including supplemental health insurance, ancillary insurance, and mental health support programs Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible employer-paid benefits spending account expenses beyond traditional benefits such as wellness, childcare, learning, and more. Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, paid volunteer time off, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. Monthly commuter stipend to help offset in-office commuting costs Click here to learn more about our Total Rewards, which vary by region and entity. If our mission energizes you and you’re ready to build the future of finance, we look forward to seeing your application.

title: Head of SOX Internal Audit
description: Cerebras Systems builds the world's largest AI chip, 56 times larger than GPUs. This architecture allows Cerebras to deliver industry-leading training and inference speeds; over 10 times faster than GPU-based hyperscale cloud inference services. This order of magnitude increase in speed is transforming the user experience of AI applications, unlocking real-time iteration and increasing intelligence via additional agentic computation. Cerebras works with the leading model labs, global enterprises, and cutting-edge AI-native startups. OpenAI recently announced a multi-year partnership https://openai.com/index/cerebras-partnership/ with Cerebras, to deploy 750 megawatts of scale, transforming key workloads with ultra high-speed inference. ABOUT THE ROLE The Head of SOX & Internal Audit will establish and lead the Company's SOX compliance program and eventually progress towards establishing the Internal Audit function. This individual will serve as a trusted advisor to executive leadership and the Audit Committee, providing independent assurance regarding the effectiveness of governance, risk management, internal controls, financial reporting processes, cybersecurity controls, and operational risk management. The successful candidate will build a scalable, risk-based Internal Audit program aligned with Institute of Internal Auditors (IIA) standards and will oversee SOX Section 404 compliance, internal control testing, deficiency remediation, and enterprise risk assessments. The role requires strong leadership, technical expertise, and the ability to partner effectively across Finance, IT, Legal, Operations, Engineering, Security, and executive management. This role aligns with Cerebras' roadmap to create clear separation between Controllership and Independent Testing and to support ongoing compliance as a public company. Key Responsibilities SOX & Internal Audit Program Leadership - Own the design, implementation, and ongoing operation of the SOX compliance program. - Lead annual SOX risk assessments, scoping, materiality considerations, and control rationalization efforts. - Oversee documentation and maintenance of narratives, flowcharts, risk-control matrices (RCMs), and process inventories. - Direct walkthroughs, control testing, deficiency evaluation, remediation validation, and management reporting. - Coordinate with Finance, IT, Legal, Security, Engineering, and business process owners to maintain effective internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR). - Monitor remediation efforts and ensure timely resolution of control deficiencies. - Drive continuous improvement through automation, control optimization, and reduction of manual testing. - Support management's SOX Sections 302 and 404 certification processes. - Establish and lead the Internal Audit function, charter, methodology, policies, and annual audit planning process. - Develop and execute a risk-based audit plan covering financial, operational, technology, cybersecurity, compliance, and strategic risks. - Present audit plans, audit results, risk assessments, and emerging risks to executive leadership and the Audit Committee. Governance, Risk, and Compliance - Assist leadership in strengthening enterprise risk management and governance processes. - Evaluate entity-level controls and the overall control environment. - Support fraud risk assessments and development of monitoring programs. - Assess risks associated with rapidly scaling AI infrastructure, data centers, supply chain operations, manufacturing, inventory management, cybersecurity, export controls, and global operations. - Review regulatory compliance programs and provide independent assurance over key compliance obligations. - Partner with Legal and Compliance functions regarding investigations, whistleblower matters, and governance initiatives. External Auditor & Audit Committee Engagement - Serve as principal liaison with external auditors on internal control, SOX, and audit matters. - Facilitate reliance strategies and coordination activities between Internal Audit and external auditors where appropriate. - Prepare Audit Committee materials and provide executive-level reporting on risks, audit findings, and remediation activities. - Support Board governance initiatives and audit committee oversight responsibilities. Organizational Development - Build a high-performing Internal Audit organization capable of supporting a public-company environment. - Develop talent, audit methodologies, and technology-enabled audit capabilities. - Champion a culture of accountability, ethical conduct, control awareness, and continuous improvement. Internal Audit Leadership - Ensure the Internal Audit function operates in accordance with IIA Global Internal Audit Standards. - Develop internal audit methodologies, quality assurance processes, and reporting frameworks. - Build and manage an Internal Audit team, including co-sourced providers and external consultants as needed. - Identify emerging risks

title: Compliance Officer/MLRO
description: Headquarters: Pakistan - Remote About Us Established in 2018, Bybit is one of the world’s leading cryptocurrency exchanges and digital financial platforms, serving over 80 million users across more than 200 countries and regions. Powered by world-class technology and a user-first mindset, Bybit delivers a seamless ecosystem across trading, payments, wealth management, custody, institutional services, and Web3 — connecting users to the future of digital finance. Our core values define how we build. We listen, care and improve to create products and experiences that put users first. Backed by a global team of ambitious builders, problem-solvers, and innovators, we foster a high-performance and fast-moving environment where talent is empowered to drive real impact at the global scale. Supported by 24/7 multilingual customer service and a strong commitment to innovation, we are shaping the future of finance through technology, collaboration, and bold execution. Today, Bybit is recognized as one of the most trusted and transparent platforms in the digital asset industry, continuing to expand its global presence while building the infrastructure for the next generation of financial services. Role Purpose Lead the establishment and ongoing oversight of the Pakistan entity’s independent Compliance function and Anti-Money Laundering, Counter-Terrorist Financing and Counter-Proliferation Financing (AML/CFT/CPF) framework. During the pre-licensing phase, the role holder will lead Compliance-owned licensing deliverables, develop the local control framework and assess operational readiness. Following licensing, the role holder will discharge the entity’s CO/MLRO responsibilities, advise the Board and senior management, and maintain effective engagement with PVARA, the Financial Monitoring Unit (FMU) and other relevant authorities. The role combines CO and MLRO responsibilities, subject to applicable regulatory requirements and any required regulatory acceptance or approval. The suitability of the combined arrangement will be reviewed periodically, considering independence, conflicts, capacity, resources and the entity’s nature, scale and complexity. Key Responsibilities Licensing and Operational Readiness Lead Compliance-owned components of the PVARA licensing application and coordinate relevant inputs from Legal, Business, Risk, Finance, Operations and Technology. Develop and maintain a regulatory obligations register, licensing deliverables tracker and local implementation roadmap. Assess gaps between group policies, systems and controls and applicable Pakistan requirements; oversee localisation and track remediation. Establish local Compliance and AML/CFT/CPF policies, governance arrangements, escalation procedures and regulatory reporting processes. Define local control requirements for customer onboarding, transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, Travel Rule compliance and suspicious transaction reporting. Assess the suitability and readiness of local, group-provided and outsourced controls, including relevant pre-launch testing. Provide a documented Compliance and AML readiness assessment to the appropriate governance forum, escalating unresolved material gaps before launch. Compliance Oversight Establish, administer and maintain a documented, risk-based Compliance Management System (CMS) proportionate to the entity’s activities and risk profile. Advise the Board, relevant committees and senior management on applicable legal and regulatory requirements, licence conditions and regulatory developments. Develop and execute a risk-based Compliance Monitoring and Testing Plan; document findings, agree remediation ownership and deadlines with accountable functions, independently validate closure, and escalate overdue or inadequate remediation. Oversee compliance with applicable conduct, customer protection, complaints-handling, client-asset and market-integrity requirements, according to the entity’s licensed activities. Review proposed products, services and material business changes from a local compliance perspective, identifying requirements, restrictions and necessary controls. Ensure material non-compliance is investigated, promptly escalated and remediated, and notified to PVARA where required. Maintain regulatory submission and commitment trackers, overseeing timely and accurate Compliance-owned responses and escalating dependency risks. Act as the primary Compliance liaison with PVARA for supervisory engagement, inspections and information requests. Develop and oversee Compliance training for employees, senior management and relevant key individuals. AML /CFT/CPF and Financial Crime Establish, implement and maintain the entity’s AML/CFT/CPF framework, aligned with applicable Pakistan legislation, regulatory requirements and relevant directions or guidance. Lead the enterprise-wide financial crime risk assessment and oversee risk-based mitigation measures. Oversee customer due diligence, beneficial ownership identification, customer risk assessment, enhanced due diligence and ongoing monitoring. Oversee transaction monitoring, sanctions screening and targeted financial sanctions controls, including escalation and action on relevant alerts. Oversee virtual asset-specific controls, including blockchain analytics, risks associated with unhosted wallets and Travel Rule compliance where applicable. Receive and assess internal suspicious activity referrals, determine whether external reporting is required, and submit suspicious transaction reports to the FMU within applicable deadlines. Exercise independent judgement on suspicious transaction reporting without requiring business approval, while maintaining confidentiality and preventing tipping-off. Manage the entity’s FMU/goAML registration, access arrangements and reporting processes, as applicable. Ensure required customer, transaction and investigation records are retained for applicable periods and remain accessible and retrievable. Liaise with the FMU and other competent authorities on financial crime matters and oversee relevant information requests. Oversee AML/CFT/CPF training and awareness, tailored to employees’ responsibilities and exposure to risk. Governance, Reporting and Control Assurance Provide periodic reports to the Board or designated committee on Compliance and AML/CFT/CPF effectiveness, material risks, incidents, findings and remediation progress. Escalate urgent or material matters promptly rather than waiting for scheduled reporting. Attend relevant Board and committee meetings and provide independent advice and challenge. Assess and oversee group-provided and outsourced Compliance/AML services, including local regulatory suitability, service standards, data access, management information and escalation arrangements. Oversee delegated Compliance and AML/CFT/CPF activities and remain accountable for discharging the CO/MLRO responsibilities, without displacing the responsibilities of the entity, Board, senior management or operational control owners. Coordinate with Risk and Internal Audit, while preserving the distinction between Compliance oversight and independent audit assurance. Support periodic review of the role holder’s continuing fitness, propriety and suitability, including the required review of the MLRO appointment. Maintain effective handover and suitably qualified cover arrangements for absences, consistent with applicable regulatory requirements. Qualifications and Experience Essential A degree in law, finance, business or a related discipline, or an equivalent relevant professional qualification. At least eight years’ relevant Compliance and/or AML/CFT experience in financial services, including at least three years in a senior Compliance, MLRO or equivalent leadership role. Strong knowledge of Pakistan’s financial regulatory and AML/CFT framework, including the Virtual Assets Act, applicable PVARA regulations, the Anti-Money Laundering Act and FMU reporting requirements. Demonstrable understanding of virtual asset business models and their financial crime, conduct and operational risks. Practical experience with customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, sanctions screening, investigations and suspicious transaction reporting. Experience developing risk assessments, policies, monitoring programmes and Board-level reporting. Ability to translate regulatory requirements into workable business, operational and technology controls. Be resident in Pakistan by the date of the formal CO/MLRO appointment and maintain residency as required under applicable regulations. Fluency in English and Urdu. Desirable Professional certification such as CAMS, an ICA qualification or an equivalent Compliance/AML credential. Experience in virtual assets, exchanges, fintech or digital financial services. Experience supporting a regulatory licence application or establishing a local Compliance function. Experience engaging with PVARA, FMU, SECP, SBP or other relevant Pakistani authorities. Familiarity with blockchain analytics tools and Travel Rule solutions. Experience overseeing centralised group services and outsourced control arrangements. Key Competencies Independence, integrity and sound judgement. Confidence to challenge senior management constructively. Clear communication with regulators, the Board and cross-functional teams. Strong analytical, investigative and problem-solving skills. Effective prioritisation in a developing regulatory environment. Ability to build a local control framework while working within a global organisation. Authority and Independence Direct access to the local Board or designated committee, including the ability to escalate without prior management clearance. Timely and unrestricted access to relevant records, systems, personnel and management information necessary to discharge the role, subject to applicable confidentiality and data-handling requirements. Adequate resources and suitably qualified support proportionate to the entity’s activities and risk profile. No client-facing, sales or other responsibilities that compromise independence, create material conflicts or impair CO/MLRO duties. Remuneration arrangements that do not link the role holder’s performance to sales or revenue targets. Group reporting arrangements that do not restrict local regulatory accountability, Board access or independent MLRO decision-making. Board oversight of appointment, replacement and removal, with regulatory approvals or notifications completed as applicable. Regulatory Appointment Conditions The role holder must satisfy applicable fitness and propriety, residency, employment, competence and regulatory appointment requirements at appointment and on an ongoing basis. Any required PVARA approval, acceptance or notification must be completed in accordance with the applicable framework. Why Join Us At Bybit, we are committed to fostering a supportive and enriching work environment. Our benefits include: - Study Growth Fund: We support your professional development and continuous learning. - Internal Events: Participate in regular team-building activities, workshops, and events designed to promote collaboration and innovation. - Global Collaboration: Be part of a diverse, international team, working alongside colleagues from around the world. - Career Advancement: Access opportunities for growth and advancement within a rapidly expanding global company. - Internal Mobility: Grow with us- Your long-term development is important to us. We offer internal job opportunities to help build your career path. To apply: https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs/bybit-compliance-officer-mlro

title: Finance Systems Production Support Lead
description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Finance systems are critical to how Anthropic operates and scales. As the Finance Systems Production Support Lead, you will set the strategy for how we support those systems, bringing operational rigor and one consistent support model across the finance portfolio. You will lead a lean support team with US and international coverage, set the service levels Finance can rely on, and make sure each incident leaves the systems stronger than it found them. This is also a chance to redefine what production support looks like, using Claude to scale and transform how we support finance systems. Claude will handle more of the routine work over time, and you will own the exceptions, the quality bar and the patterns that feed back into the product roadmap. This team will cover our core platforms, including homegrown systems and applications built on Claude. Responsibilities Own the support model: Build one operating model for tickets, access and incidents across finance applications, including ERP, close, procure to pay, revenue, planning, tax and treasury systems, plus new internally built applications. Lead a lean support team: Manage the support team day to day, including capacity, performance and escalation paths. You will also be the team's backup, working tickets and incidents yourself as needed. Design the rotation and operating rigor: Design the US and international support rotation, including close-week coverage and handoffs. Set the routines that keep support consistent, such as triage, runbooks, postmortems and regular service reviews. Drive operational excellence: Shape lean, scalable support processes that grow with the business, and implement leading practices across how the team works. Build training and onboarding: Create the training and onboarding that gets new support team members productive quickly and prepares Finance users for new systems and releases. Set and meet service levels: Define SLAs by priority and category, run triage, and plan coverage around month-end and quarter-end close. Run incidents and root cause analysis: Lead sensitive and time-critical production issues from first response to communication with Finance leaders, then drive root causes to a fix so they don't recur. Own release management: Run release testing and deployment across the portfolio, including Workday's twice-yearly releases. Partner with Product Owners on what to test, and put test automation ahead of added headcount. Run support by the metrics: Report ticket volume, time to resolve, SLA attainment, defects that escape a release, and automation coverage. Use the data to drive decisions, and turn the trends into input for each product roadmap. Make support audit-ready: Work with Product Owners and Internal Audit so tickets, access changes, support-run changes and runbooks hold up to SOX and public company expectations. Run recurring user access reviews: Own the recurring user access review cycle across finance applications, with evidence that stands up to audit. Minimum qualifications Experience running production support for enterprise finance applications, ideally including Workday Financials or a comparable ERP, in a live, high-volume environment Experience leading a lean support function, including coverage across time zones Experience shaping lean, scalable support processes using leading practices, including SLAs, triage, incident management, root cause analysis and runbooks, and running them with metrics that leaders actually use Knowledge of how finance works day to day, including close, procure to pay Understanding of SOX controls for change management and user access, including recurring access reviews, and the ability to produce evidence that stands up to audit Experience leading release management, including testing and deployment, with a practical view on what to automate first Ability to stay calm and clear under pressure, and to explain an incident and its risk to both accountants and engineers Hands-on skills: reading an integration error, querying data with SQL and digging into a ticket yourself when that's what it takes Excitement about using Claude and other AI tools to scale and transform how support is done, with good judgment about where a human must stay in the loop Preferred qualifications Experience with Jira Service Management, including workflows, queues and dashboards Experience supporting integrations across billing, procurement, expense, tax, planning or treasury platforms Experience with internally built finance applications or data pipelines, such as BigQuery, dbt or Airflow Experience scaling finance systems to public-company standards Wo
